question: Does hiring an agent on your marketplace beat doing the job yourself, and can you prove it?

venues: Venus Core Pool (BSC) — vUSDT and vUSDC, verified three ways

two venues: PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% · 0x36696169C63e42cd08ce11f5deeBbCeBae652050 vs PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.25% · 0x1401ff943D08a7E098328C1d3a9d388923B115D2 — depth and the flow screen chose the same one

tasks.task: Earn — fees on a liquidity position
tasks.metric: net return on capital (fees − realized convexity cost − costs), P25–P75
tasks.without_agent: mint once at the same width, never touch it (passive_policy)
tasks.verdict: agent loses to DIY by 64.29pp, bands do not overlap

tasks.task: Protect — avoid being picked off by one-way flow
tasks.metric: net return on capital, P25–P75 (the cost of the withdrawals is charged in full)

primary_metric.name: realized convexity cost (upper bound on LVR)
primary_metric.summary: realized convexity cost (upper bound on LVR): 0.000464581 vs 0.00854537 — 18.4x better

tasks.without_agent: the same wide band, held through everything (withdrawal disabled)
tasks.with_agent: Sentinel — withdraw on §3.4 toxicity, re-enter after m_clear
tasks.verdict: agent loses to DIY by 38.17pp, bands do not overlap

tasks.task: Choose — which pool to provide liquidity to
tasks.venue: two venues: PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% · 0x36696169C63e42cd08ce11f5deeBbCeBae652050 vs PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.25% · 0x1401ff943D08a7E098328C1d3a9d388923B115D2 — depth and the flow screen chose the same one
tasks.metric: net return on capital of the same agent on the chosen venue, P25–P75. Capital for this task is 0.03181, not the report's 1. A1's ceiling is eps x pool liquidity and therefore a property of the pool, and the shallower venue binds it — PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% · 0x36696169C63e42cd08ce11f5deeBbCeBae652050: 7.031 · PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.25% · 0x1401ff943D08a7E098328C1d3a9d388923B115D2: 0.06362 (at 0.5x margin). Both columns run at the same figure, because a comparison between two venues at two capitals is partly a comparison between two position sizes.
tasks.without_agent: pick the deepest pool — PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% · 0x36696169C63e42cd08ce11f5deeBbCeBae652050, 84.0x the median liquidity (the obvious heuristic: more TVL is safer)
tasks.with_agent: pick the pool whose flow is not one-way — PancakeSwap v3 WBNB/USDT 0.05% · 0x36696169C63e42cd08ce11f5deeBbCeBae652050, where §3.4's imbalance arm fires on 41.9% of samples against 42.8% on the other — which is the pool depth chose too
tasks.verdict: indistinguishable: +0.00pp is below the 0.10pp materiality floor

tasks.task: Route — which lending venue to supply to
tasks.venue: Venus Core Pool (BSC) — vUSDT and vUSDC, verified three ways
tasks.metric: net return on supplied capital (realized yield - switch costs), P25-P75, over a 168h stated holding period. Capital for this task is $10,000 of stablecoin, not the report's figure — that one is denominated in WBNB and means nothing to a lending market.

primary_metric.name: moves made (best rate seen 2.98%, hurdle 1.06%, break-even at 2 days)
primary_metric.summary: moves made (best rate seen 2.98%, hurdle 1.06%, break-even at 2 days): 2 vs 1 — worse

tasks.without_agent: supply to the highest-rate venue once and never move (park_policy)
tasks.with_agent: Router - move only when the rate edge clears the round-trip cost
tasks.note: net return on supplied capital (realized yield − switch costs)
tasks.verdict: indistinguishable: -0.01pp is below the 0.10pp materiality floor
